terra.problem: The passage says Joash did right throughout Jehoiada’s days. It does not say here that he stopped doing right before the end of his reign.
The joke about hearing slower news does not clearly connect to the Levites’ slow action.
The text places the chest at the gate, but does not say everybody walked by it.
The passage does not locate the altar or say nobody had to look for the chest.
The drawer joke assumes the baker knows Papa Dorin’s backstory. It does not establish that he lived in a drawer.
The Levites’ failure to make haste does not establish that they hesitated. The officers’ and people’s rejoicing does not establish how quickly they acted either.
The text says the chest contained a large amount when it was emptied; it does not say it became full again and again.
The passage does not list singers, gatekeepers or musicians among the workers hired for repairs. It does not establish that none had any role in the job.
The passage says the workers restored and reinforced the house. It does not say they completed the restoration before reinforcing it.
The passage shows Jehoiada working with Joash on the repairs, but does not establish that he had been working with him all along.
The explanation simply quotes and repeats the facts. Apart from calling the baker friend, it has little of Papa Dorin’s voice.
Regular offerings do not necessarily mean offerings day after day; the text does not specify their frequency.
The text says the offerings were presented regularly, but does not specify a schedule or say Jehoiada’s days were busy.
The text says the offerings were regular, not that they were presented out in the open.
The passage does not establish that Jehoiada worked beside Joash for all those years.
The passage identifies Jehoiada as a priest, but does not explicitly say he was never a king.
